A1.justification: Both complete 21-page PDFs describe MotionMAR and include Appendices A-C. Text and rendered-page comparisons identify differences only in the arXiv version/date stamp and eight numerical entries in Table 6.

before.justification: v1 reports original AMASS and GORP motion-reconstruction results, real-world qualitative evaluations, computational measurements, and extensive ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, with revised SAGE (TMT) scores in the appendix's Table 6.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1-3 retain identical tokenization, scale-aware control, autoregressive generation, refinement, and training procedures. The revised scores do not document a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same AMASS subsets and tracker scenarios, GORP motion-controller subset, and real-world examples. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every comparison. Table 6 retains SAGE, SAGE (TMT), and MotionMAR; only SAGE (TMT)'s scores change.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, S1-S3 configurations, metrics, training settings, and appendix protocols are unchanged. No setting change or experimental rerun is documented for the revised Table 6 values.

E4.justification: Table 6 revises the evidence about transferring TMT into SAGE: reconstruction benefits become smaller, and the jitter benefit becomes a disadvantage. The ablation's stated design and all other ablations, sensitivity analyses, and failure cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Table 6 still supplies point estimates, without added run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Only Table 6's SAGE (TMT) row changes: MPJRE 2.39 to 2.47, MPJPE 2.83 to 3.14, MPJVE 16.36 to 20.01, Hand PE 0.84 to 0.95, Upper PE 1.22 to 1.30, Lower PE 5.14 to 5.79, Root PE 2.58 to 2.87, and Jitter 5.36 to 7.44. Jitter now exceeds SAGE's unchanged 6.55. MotionMAR's results and all other result entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Equations 1-10, and appendix complexity reasoning are identical. No definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about temporal hierarchical modeling, the proposed modules, and reconstruction performance.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 still says TMT slightly improves SAGE's reconstruction while remaining inferior to MotionMAR. It does not discuss the revised jitter disadvantage. All mechanism explanations and appendix limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B-C, Table 14, architectural specifications, optimization details, hardware information, and the source-code access link are unchanged. No explanation of the numerical replacement is provided.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and novelty positioning are identical.

P1.justification: The arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 22 June 2026 to v2 dated 6 August 2026. Manuscript prose, headings, terminology, and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, formatting, and placement are unchanged. Table 6 substitutes numerical values without changing its display; the updated version/date stamp is the only other visible difference.

improvement.justification: The revised Table 6 row no longer exactly duplicates the separate SO(3) ablation in Table 13, suggesting a possible reporting correction. However, neither PDF explains the replacement, and the discussion remains unchanged despite the newly reported jitter disadvantage. With the method and remaining evidence unchanged, the PDFs do not establish whether this localized revision improves reporting accuracy or overall quality.
